newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RETAIL PETROL PRICE ROSE 2 PCT, MAY GO UP.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RETAIL PETROL PRICE ROSE 2 PCT, MAY GO UP.

text.p: Retail prices of petrol rose in Poland by nearly two percent on the average last week and may go up a bit more next week, following increases by producers, an agency monitoring the fuels market said on Thursday.

"All brands of petrol increased on the average by three groszes (0.03 zloty), a little less than two percent, while the price of diesel fuel rose by one grosz, which is less than one percent," Michal Bichniewicz of Brog Services told Reuters.
In the middle of this week unleaded E-95 petrol cost 1.71 zlotys per litre, unleaded E-98 1.85 zloty and leaded E-98 1.83 zloty, he said.
He said the petrol price were likely to go up by between one and two groszes next week.

Pol and's two biggest producers, Petrochemia Plock and Rafineria Gdansk, has increased wholesale prices of petrol by between four to five groszes on the average and wholesale price of diesel by two to three groszes.
The firms, which cover 80 percent of Poland's demand for petrol, said the hikes resulted from high world oil price and strengthening dollar.
